finding.claim: getActualArrayKey() evals token text from the scanned PHP file. The allowlist and callback guard don't stop a parenthesised callable expression such as ('system')('id') as an array key, so scanning a crafted file runs attacker-chosen commands in the PHPCS process.
finding.source: Array key tokens in the PHP file being linted (attacker-controlled when phpcs runs on untrusted code, e.g. fork PRs or third-party repos). Read via $this->tokens at lines 491-593.
finding.sink: @eval('return ' . $content . ';' . PHP_EOL) at line 598, with $content built from source tokens.

trace.note: Public getActualArrayKey(); downstream sniffs call it on array items. No in-tree callers, so reach depends on those sniffs.
Loop over key tokens from firstNonEmpty to lastNonEmpty.
Non-special tokens are appended verbatim to $content, so ( and ) survive.
Allowlist check: tokens are accepted if present in $acceptedTokens.
Tokens::$bracketTokens is merged into the allowlist, admitting ( and ). Per the BCTokens docblock this covers parentheses; the PHPCS Tokens class is not in this tree, so this is unverified.

Callback guard bails only when the token immediately before ( is a T_CONSTANT_ENCAPSED_STRING (or heredoc/nowdoc end). In ('system')('id') the token before the second ( is ), so the guard does not fire.
eval() runs the reconstructed expression. @ only silences warnings; the catch blocks at 599-605 handle exceptions, not execution.

finding.guards_checked: (1) Token allowlist at 116-125 and 157-165: no identifiers, variables, or T_STRING, so named functions and variables are blocked, but the ( ) pair is admitted. (2) Callback guard at 568-574: covers 'name'( but not )( or ('name')(. (3) Comment/whitespace skipping at 495-502: no effect on exploitability. (4) Heredoc handling at 577-591: not on this path. (5) try/catch at 596-605: does not prevent execution. (6) Decoy 25 (identifier allowlist) does not match, because the attacker can compose expressions from literals and parentheses. Decoy 22 (template compile) is not relevant.
